title: Newsletter preference is not round-trippable from GET /config

evidence.quote: newsletters_enabled: bool | None = Field(default=None, description="Enable newsletter integration")

reasoning: The API accepts newsletters_enabled as a synced configuration setting, and get_config documents that it returns all synced settings, but ConfigResponse has no raw newsletters_enabled field. The only related response value is newsletters.enabled, which combines the stored preference with whether the Gmail integration is configured. When Gmail is not configured, stored true and false both serialize as false, so clients cannot read back or sync the actual user preference.
reproduction: Set newsletters_enabled=true in the database or via PUT /api/config while newsletter_service.is_configured is false, then GET /api/config. The response reports newsletters.enabled=false and provides no field that preserves the stored true value.
recommendation: Add an explicit newsletters_enabled field to ConfigResponse and populate it from config.newsletters_enabled. Keep newsletters.enabled as integration status if clients need both concepts.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no linked tests. The repo tests that touch /api/config assert cover key masking and PDF settings, but they do not assert newsletter preference round-tripping or the distinction between stored preference and integration availability.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a GET /api/config test that sets newsletters_enabled to both true and false while the newsletter service is unconfigured, and assert the raw newsletters_enabled response field matches the stored value.
minimumFixScope: app/api/config.py response schema and _config_to_response mapping; update/extend config endpoint tests.
